title: Ottavia M. Epifania
text:
The horror persists, and so do I.
  
  

I am a tenure-track researcher in psychometrics at the Department of Psychology and Cognitive Science of the University of Trento, in Rovereto.
I work on latent variable models, mostly Item Response Theory: how to shorten a test without losing what it measures, how to generate test items automatically, and how to model accuracy and response times in implicit measures. Most of this ends up as R packages and Shiny apps, so that other people can use it too.
I am part of the core team of Psicostat and an Academic Editor at PeerJ.

title: Software
text:
Item Response Theory procedures for building tests from an item bank and for developing short forms of full-length tests. They differ in how much control you have over the latent trait levels you target, and in whether the number of items is set in advance or chosen by the algorithm.

title: Software
text:
implicitMeasures
Scores for the Implicit Association Test and the Single Category IAT, with functions for preparing the data, plotting the results and tabulating descriptive statistics.
CRAN · GitHub · Paper

title: Software
text:
matRiks
Raven-like matrices of 4 or 9 cells, generated from logical and visual-spatial rules, each with a response list of the correct answer and 10 distractors. Maintained by Andrea Brancaccio; developed within the PRIN 2020 project on adaptive assessment of executive functions and fluid intelligence.
CRAN · GitHub · Tutorial
